Regulatory Compliance
Pursuant to the amendments introduced under the Finance Act, 2019, and the subsequent notification issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in August 2019, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) have been classified as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) for regulatory purposes and are consequently brought under the direct regulatory purview of the RBI. Nevertheless, the National Housing Bank (NHB) continues to exercise supervisory oversight over HFCs. In line with this regulatory framework, the Master Direction titled “Non-Banking Financial Company – Housing Finance Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2021” was issued on February 17, 2021, thereby superseding the regulations and directions previously prescribed under Chapter XVII.
The Company diligently complies with the guidelines, circulars, 
and directions issued by the RBI/NHB from time to time. The Company has ensured full compliance with the following regulatory frameworks:
•
Master 
Direction – Non-Banking Financial Company
– Housing Finance Company (Reserve Bank) 
Directions, 2025;
•Master Direction 
– Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking
Financial Company – Scale Based Regulation)Directions, 2025Additionally, the Company has complied with all directions 
and guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). These include, inter alia, regulations relating to acceptance of deposits, accounting standards, prudential norms, capital adequacy requirements, credit ratings, corporate governance practices, liquidity management, information technology framework, fair practices code, fraud monitoring mechanisms, concentration of investments, risk management systems, capital market exposure norms, Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements, maintenance of the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), and anti-money laundering (AML) measures.
Your Company has been maintaining capital adequacy ratio as 
prescribed by the RBI. The capital adequacy ratio was 25.48 percent as on 31
st March, 2026, as against 23.20 percent 
as on 31st March, 2025 (as against the regulatory minimum 
of 15 percent).
The Company has consistently complied with the directions, 
guidelines, and circulars issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), National Housing Bank (NHB), and Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as applicable to a listed entity and an Upper Layer Non-Banking Financial Company (Housing Finance Company). Regulatory and statutory updates are periodically placed before the Board, and the Company has implemented robust systems and processes to ensure ongoing compliance with all applicable requirements.
In accordance with the requirements of the Reserve Bank 
of India’s Scale Based Regulations, the Company has implemented the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP). The ICAAP Policy was approved by the Board of Directors on 7
th March, 2024, and the implementation of the 
ICAAP framework has been completed on 2nd August, 2024.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), through Circular No. RBI/2023-24/117 dated January 31, 2024, as extended thereafter, has mandated all regulated entities (REs) to implement streamlined internal compliance monitoring functions leveraging technology by April 30, 2025. The circular emphasizes the adoption of a comprehensive, integrated, enterprise-wide, and workflow-based compliance management system to enhance monitoring efficiency and minimize manual intervention. In line with these regulatory expectations, adherence to this regulatory requirement, the Company has developed a Compliance Testing Tool designed to track all applicable regulatory and legal compliances, thereby improving oversight and reducing dependency on manual processes. This tool is in its initial phase of adoption and is evolving within the organisation with the increasing awareness amongst the employees who are being trained to effectively integrate this tool into their compliance routines.

Management perspective about future of the Company
Over the past decade, India’s housing finance market has expanded steadily, supported by sustained housing demand, improving affordability and a favourable policy environment. Rising aspirations for home ownership, expanding urban centres and greater access to formal credit continue to strengthen the sector’s long-term fundamentals.
Valued at approximately ` 44.4 trillion as of March 2026, 
India’s housing finance market is well positioned for sustained 
long-term expansion, supported by structural growth drivers such as rapid urbanisation, rising household incomes, favourable demographics, increasing formalisation of credit and continued government support for housing.
Against this backdrop, the Company continues to strengthen 
its position in the housing finance sector through disciplined portfolio growth, improved asset quality and stable Net Interest Margins. Leveraging its extensive branch network, a strong agency force of over 8,500 marketing intermediaries, developer connectors and strategic partnerships, the Company is widening its reach across Tier II and Tier III markets while reinforcing its retail franchise. Continued emphasis on recovery, delinquency management and portfolio monitoring remains central to preserving asset quality.
Technology continues to be a key enabler of the Company’s 
long-term strategy. Through Project RED, the Company is modernising its operating model by strengthening digital loan origination, customer onboarding, servicing and analytics-led decision-making. Continuous enhancements to the HomY application, greater adoption of digital onboarding, process automation and improved turnaround times are expected to enhance customer experience while improving operational efficiency and scalability.
Going forward, the Company will continue to expand its 
retail portfolio with greater emphasis on higher-yielding products while broadening its presence across emerging customer segments. It also remains committed to supporting affordable housing through the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) and developing solutions aligned with the evolving financing requirements of salaried, self-employed and first-time homebuyers.
Alongside growth, the Company will continue to optimise 
its borrowing profile to maintain a competitive cost of funds, strengthen Net Interest Margins and improve overall 
profitability. Robust underwriting standards, prudent treasury management, continuous portfolio surveillance and proactive recovery mechanisms under the SARFAESI Act and other statutory frameworks will remain integral to the Company’s risk management approach.
Supported by a trusted brand, one of the industry’s 
widest distribution networks, strong parentage and a technology-enabled operating platform, the Company remains well-positioned to capitalise on the long-term opportunities in India’s expanding housing finance market while creating sustainable value for all stakeholders.

Succession Planning:
In furtherance of the Company’s commitment to business 
continuity, leadership stability, and the effective execution of 
its long-term strategic objectives, the Board has established 
a structured succession planning framework for senior 
leadership positions. To ensure a smooth and seamless 
leadership transition with minimal operational disruption, 
the Board has resolved that the incoming Managing Director 
& Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO) shall be appointed 
well in advance, preferably 4 to 6 months prior to formally 
assuming office.
Pursuant to Article 138(b) of the Articles of Association 
of the Company, LIC of India is entitled to nominate up to 
one-third of the total strength of the Board of Directors of the 
Company. Accordingly, the Board, after due consideration, 
approved the deputation of a senior official from LIC of 
India as its Nominee for the position of Chief Operating 
Officer (COO) as part of the succession planning process 
for the office of the Managing Director & CEO. This initiative 
is aimed at ensuring continuity, organizational stability, 
and effective implementation of the Company’s long-term 
business strategies within a reasonable transition period, generally ranging from four to six months prior to the 
cessation of the incumbent Managing Director & CEO.
In accordance with the said policy and in view of the impending 
superannuation of Shri T Adhikari the Managing Director & Chief 
Executive Officer of the Company from the services of LIC of 
India, the Board had, during the year, appointed Dr. Sanjay Dayal 
as the Chief Operating Officer to facilitate a smooth leadership 
transition in line with the Company’s succession framework. 
However, following his sad and untimely demise on May 9, 
2026, he ceased to hold the office of Chief Operating Officer. 
Thereafter, pursuant to the deputation by Life Insurance 
Corporation of India and based on the recommendation of 
the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board 
approved the appointment of Shri Sandeep Kumar as the 
Chief Operating Officer. His appointment forms an integral 
part of the Company’s succession planning framework and 
is intended to ensure continuity of leadership, operational 
stability and seamless transition in the management of the 
affairs of the Company.
Further, in terms of the Regulation 17 (4) of the SEBI (LODR), 
2015 the Company has adopted a succession planning policy 
for its Key Managerial and senior management personnel 
which has been hosted on the website of the Company on the

Internal Financial Control Systems and their Adequacy:
The Company has implemented a comprehensive internal financial control framework that is commensurate with the nature, scale, and complexity of its operations. These controls are considered adequate and have been operating effectively throughout the period.
The Board of Directors confirms that the Company 
has established a robust internal control framework commensurate with the scale and complexity of its operations. Detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Risk Control Matrices have been implemented to provide reasonable assurance over the accuracy and reliability of financial reporting, as well as compliance with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. These controls are continuously monitored and periodically reviewed to ensure their ongoing adequacy, effectiveness, and alignment with 
evolving business needs.
To further strengthen its internal control framework, the 
Company periodically engages independent external experts to perform objective evaluations of its control systems. The recommendations and best practices arising from these assessments are thoroughly reviewed by the Management and the Audit Committee, and are systematically implemented to support continuous improvement and enhance operational effectiveness.

Annexure 1 to this report.
Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy:
The Company has established a comprehensive Whistle Blower Policy that provides employees and other stakeholders with a formal channel to report concerns pertaining to matters covered under the policy. The policy promotes the reporting of genuine concerns and grievances while ensuring adequate protection against any form of retaliation or victimization of whistle blowers. Additionally, it provides direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee, thereby strengthening transparency, accountability, and the integrity of the reporting process.
The Whistle Blower Policy, forming an integral part of the 
Company’s Vigil Mechanism, is reviewed periodically on an annual basis or in line with applicable regulatory changes, as required. During the year, the Board reviewed and approved certain amendments to the policy. The revised policy aims to further enhance the existing framework by promoting a secure and transparent environment that encourages individuals to report concerns in confidence, while ensuring adequate safeguards against victimisation.
During the period under review no concerns or grievances 
were reported under Vigil Mechanism/ Whistle Blower Policy.

Cyber Security
The Company has established a Board-approved Cyber Security Policy that defines the overarching framework for cyber risk management and resilience, in alignment with applicable regulatory guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank 
of India (RBI). The policy is supported by detailed internal standards, procedures, and control frameworks designed to ensure consistent implementation and governance across the organization.
The Company has adopted a risk-based approach to cyber 
security and has implemented industry-aligned technologies and controls to support its digital initiatives. These controls are integrated with well-defined processes to safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets, and to protect the Company’s network, endpoints, and data from unauthorized access and cyber threats.
A multi-layered security architecture has been deployed, 
incorporating preventive, detective, and responsive controls. This includes the use of advanced threat intelligence platforms to enable proactive identification, monitoring, and mitigation of both internal and external threats. The Company has further implemented security solutions such as next-generation firewalls, endpoint detection and response (EDR), security monitoring systems, and deception technologies, which collectively enhance its cyber defence capabilities.
The Company has also established continuous monitoring, 
incident response, and vulnerability management practices to ensure timely detection and mitigation of cyber risks. Regular security assessments, including vulnerability assessments and penetration testing, are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of controls and to address emerging threats. Cyber resilience is integrated with the Company’s Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery frameworks to ensure operational continuity in the event of cyber incidents.
To strengthen the human element of cyber security, the 
Company conducts periodic cyber security awareness programs for employees and stakeholders. In addition, the technology and information security teams undergo ongoing training and capability-building initiatives to stay abreast of evolving threat landscapes, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.

ANNEXURE 1 
TO THE BOARD’S REPORT.
NOTE ON INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROL
1. Background: As per the Section 134(5)(e) of the
Companies 
Act 2013, the Directors’ Responsibility
Statement referred to in sub-section (3)(c) shall statethat “the directors, in the case of a listed company, hadlaid down internal financial controls to be followed by thecompany and that such internal financial controls areadequate and were operating effectively.”
Explanation: For the purposes of this clause, the term 
“internal financial controls” means the policies and procedures adopted by the company for ensuring the orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including adherence to company’s policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention and detection of frauds and errors, the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records, and the timely preparation of reliable financial information.
2.
P
olicies and Procedures: The Company has laid down
relevant policies and procedures. As part of the InternalControl Framework (ICF), the Company has in placestandard operating procedures (SOP) covering the keyactivities / functions / processes (Retail Loans, ProjectLoans, Borrowings, Treasury, Accounting etc.)
3.
Compliance 
Reporting: The Company has in place
process to ensure compliance with the provisions of allapplicable laws and the same is reported in the form ofquarterly compliance reports by the process owners tothe MD & CEO as well as to the Board.
4.
Risk Management System: 
The Company has in place
an Enterprise Risk Management Policy which providesa framework to address the risk faced by the Companyon a sustainable basis. The risk management functionwithin the Company is responsible for review of existingrisks and identifying potential risks and risk mitigationmeasures. There is a system of quarterly reporting tothe Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee andthe Board. Apart from the Enterprise Risk Management Policy, the company also maintains IFC documentation in the form of Risk Control Matrix (RCM), Entity Level Controls (ELC) and Financial Closure and Reporting process (FCRP) which forms the basis of IFC Testing.
5.
Inter
nal Audit System: The Internal Audit process
determines the existence, adequacy, effectiveness andadherence to the Company’s internal controls, besidesreview of processes, adherence to SOP and compliancewith statutory provisions/ regulatory guidelines.The Internal Audit Department conducts the internalaudit of the Back Offices and Corporate Office, exceptfor certain specific areas within the Corporate Officeaudit that require specialized domain expertise. In thisregard, two independent firms of Chartered Accountantswere engaged as experts with the approval of theAudit Committee.
6.
Adequacy 
and Effectiveness of Internal Financial

9.  Specify the reason(s),  if the company has failed to spend two per cent of the average net profit as per sub-section (5)
of section 135:
The Company is committed to supporting impactful projects and partners exclusively with credible implementation agencies 
that possess a strong track record. CSR initiatives are carried out through a structured disbursement process, whichincludes rigorous monitoring and verification to ensure the efficient use of funds by implementation partners. Under thistranche-based system, partial payments have been released, with the remaining funds scheduled for disbursement as perthe approved project work plans. This method ensures the effective execution of CSR projects sanctioned by LIC HFL CSR, fostering sustainable community development and upholding the organization’s core values. In the financial year 2025–26, the Company undertook thorough evaluation and processing of received contribution requests and remains committed tooptimizing the impact of its CSR funds.

LIC Housing Finance Limited (LICHFL), incorporated in 1989, is  
one of India’s largest and most trusted housing finance companies, dedicated to enabling affordable home ownership and improving access to housing finance across the country. With the core objective of providing long-term financial assistance for the purchase and construction of residential houses and flats, the company has played a significant role in supporting individuals and families in achieving housing security and financial stability.
Over the years, LICHFL has expanded its portfolio beyond housing 
loans to include loans against existing property for business and personal requirements. The company also provides financial assistance to professionals for the establishment and expansion of clinics, nursing homes, diagnostic centres, office spaces, and the procurement of equipment. In addition, LICHFL extends project finance support to builders and developers engaged in the construction of residential housing projects, thereby contributing to the growth of the housing sector in India.
The company went public in 1994, and its shares have since 
been actively listed and traded on the NSE and BSE. Backed by a strong institutional foundation, extensive distribution network, customer-centric approach, and proven industry expertise, LICHFL has established itself as a respected and reliable financial services institution. As one of the pioneers in India’s housing finance sector, the company takes pride in having served over 25 lakh prudent homeowners, contributing significantly to inclusive growth, improved living standards, and socio-economic development across urban and rural communities.INTRODUCTION

RESEARCH METHODOLOGY CHAPTER 2
LIC Housing Finance Ltd. commissioned Inclusive India Foundation to undertake an impact assessment study aimed at 
evaluating both the short-term outcomes and long-term sustainability of its CSR initiatives during FY 2025–26.
OBJECTIVES OF THE STUDY
To assess the immediate as well as sustained impact generated through the CSR initiatives implemented by LIC Housing Finance Ltd.To evaluate the extent to which the program has achieved its planned objectives and desired outcomes.To examine the short-term and long-term direct, indirect, and unintended effects of the intervention on beneficiaries and communities.To identify key strengths, implementation gaps, and opportunities for improving program delivery and effectiveness.To suggest strategic recommendations for strengthening the overall impact, scalability, and sustainability of the program in the future.
PROJECT EVALUATION FRAMEWORK  
After the collection of relevant information and perceptions through interviews, the OECD framework would be followed/applied. It has six evaluation criteria - relevance, coherence, efficiency, effectiveness, impact, and sustainability for each of the indicators.

USE OF MIXED METHODOLOGY FOR MAXIMUM INSIGHTS
The research problem pertained to assessing the impact of this initiative on local communities. The project's success lies 
in understanding how this initiative has positively influenced the lives of individuals within the local communities, including 
their economic well-being, social integration, and overall quality of life. It aims to measure the tangible and intangible benefits 
brought about by the initiative and evaluate its effectiveness in addressing the needs and challenges of the target population.
ENSURING TRIANGULATION
Triangulation was needed to increase the credibility and validity of the research findings. It was also a measure taken to ensure 
the trustworthiness of the research process. The findings of the quantitative research have been verified with the insights from 
qualitative research, and the report has also been structured to reflect this point.

03. SUMMARY OF REPORT
3.1 UDHYAM
IMPLEMENTING AGENCY
Lok Bharti Education Society
PROJECT BACKGROUND  
The Udyam Project is a skill development initiative implemented by Lok Bharti Education Society with support from CSR partner 
LIC Housing Finance Limited (LIC HFL), aimed at enhancing the employability and livelihood opportunities of economically weaker and unemployed respondents. The project provides structured vocational training in demand-driven trades such as masonry, electrical work, and plumbing, along with apprenticeship-based hands-on learning, soft skills, digital literacy, and financial literacy. It also includes counseling, certification, and placement support to ensure a smooth transition from training to employment or self-employment, thereby promoting sustainable income generation and socio-economic upliftment of respondents.
PROJECT DETAILS
Project DurationFY 2024 - 2025 Total Beneficiaries1,800
Project LocationsMadhya Pradesh, Satna Budget` 1,52,72,400Assessment YearFY 2025 - 2026
Alignment with SDGs
 PROJECT ACTIVITIES
The project conducted outreach and mobilization activities in rural areas through camps and community engagement to identify eligible respondents for training.
The project provided pre-admission counseling to align respondents’ skills, interests, and educational background with suitable vocational trades.The project delivered structured hands-on vocational training in trades such as masonry, electrical work, plumbing, and allied sectors.
The project 
integrated apprenticeship-based on-the-job training to ensure practical exposure and industry readiness of respondents.The project incorporated soft skills training to enhance communication, teamwork, and workplace behavior among respondents.
The project 
provided digital literacy training to improve respondents’ basic technological and operational competencies.The project conducted financial literacy sessions to strengthen respondents’ understanding of savings, budgeting, and financial management.
The project 
facilitated entrepreneurship orientation sessions to encourage self-employment and enterprise development among respondents.The project ensured placement support and linkage with local companies to enable employment opportunities for trained respondents.
The project 
organized final assessments and certification processes to validate the skill acquisition of respondents.

IMPLEMENTING AGENCY  
Rural Development Trust , BAIF ISLD, Foundation For Ecological Security (FES), AROH Foundation, Society for Development 
Alternatives, Indo-Global Social Service Society (IGSSS), NIRDESH ,Arpan Seva Sansthan, AFPRO, Appropriate Technology India (ATI), URMUL Rural Health Research and Development Trust, SAMARTHAN –Centre for Development Support, Integrated Development Foundation (IDF), National Agro Foundation, Mount Valley Development Association (MVDA), Deepak Foundation, Centre for Advanced Research and Development (CARD), Amhi Amchya Arogyasathi, Shramik Bharti.
PROJECT BACKGROUND  
The project implemented by Hriday Foundation focuses on promoting holistic rural development through integrated interventions across agriculture, livelihoods, natural resource management, health, education, and community empowerment. The initiative emphasizes sustainable agricultural practices such as organic farming, crop diversification, vermicomposting, kitchen gardens, and climate-resilient farming approaches to enhance productivity and household food security.
The project also supports water conservation and natural resource management through the development of irrigation systems, 
farm ponds, rainwater harvesting structures, groundwater recharge mechanisms, and soil-water conservation measures aimed at improving water availability and sustainable resource utilization.
To strengthen rural livelihoods, the program promotes income-generating activities including livestock rearing, poultry, dairy, 
fishery, mushroom cultivation, micro-enterprises, and skill development initiatives to enhance economic opportunities for community members. Institutional strengthening remains a key focus area through the capacity building of SHGs, FIGs, FPOs, and Village Development Committees (VDCs) through trainings, exposure visits, financial literacy programs, and market linkage support.
In the areas of health, sanitation, and education, the project facilitates health camps, nutrition awareness, menstrual hygiene 
promotion, sanitation initiatives, access to safe drinking water, and hygiene awareness activities. Educational support interventions include smart classrooms, digital learning facilities, libraries, remedial education support, Anganwadi strengthening, and improvement of school infrastructure. The project further encourages environmental sustainability through renewable energy and climate-focused interventions such as solar lighting, biogas units, smokeless cookstoves, plantation drives, and climate awareness campaigns. Community mobilization and participatory development are promoted through government convergence efforts, community participation, and strengthening local governance systems to ensure long-term sustainability and ownership.

The project aims to establish a community-driven and sustainable solid waste management system in residential, tourist, and 
ecologically sensitive regions to improve cleanliness, public health, environmental sustainability, and livelihood opportunities.

institutional systems through training of waste collectors, SHGs, and community stakeholders, along with support through PPE 
kits, waste collection vehicles, bins, operational tools, Panchayat coordination, and user fee mechanisms.

REPORT ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
The Company remains steadfast in its commitment to 
maintaining the highest standards of Corporate Governance, with regulatory compliance serving as a cornerstone of its governance framework. This commitment enables the Company to effectively address stakeholder expectations while pursuing sustainable and long-term growth. The Board, in its fiduciary capacity, exercises prudent oversight to safeguard shareholder interests, promote transparency, integrity, and ethical conduct, and ensure the establishment of robust and efficient governance processes that are responsive to the evolving business environment and stakeholder requirements.
COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CODE OF GOVERNANCE
The Company’s Corporate Governance framework comprises a comprehensive set of policies, systems, and practices aimed at reinforcing its core values of fairness, transparency, accountability, and ethical business conduct. These principles are integrated into the Company’s governance structure and operational processes, ensuring responsible decision-making and promoting long-term, sustainable value creation for all stakeholders.
The Company is committed to achieving operational excellence 
and delivering superior customer experiences across all facets of its business operations. It recognizes its responsibility towards all stakeholders, including customers, regulatory authorities, employees, and the broader community. As a responsible corporate entity, the Company conducts its affairs with integrity, ensures compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, and fosters an inclusive and empowering work environment that supports the growth and development of its employees.
The Company is committed to maintaining the highest 
standards of transparency, integrity, and ethical governance. To reinforce these values, it has established a comprehensive Code of Conduct applicable to its Directors and employees, which is available on the Company’s website. The Company ensures full compliance with the applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), and the Uniform Listing Agreement entered into with the Stock Exchanges. Further, the Company adheres to the relevant provisions of the Reserve Bank of India’s Master Direction – the Reserve Bank of India (Housing Finance Companies) Directions, 2025 and the Guidelines and Circulars issued thereunder from time to time and the Master Direction-The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Registration, Exemptions and 
Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025 and the Guidelines and Circulars issued thereunder from time to time. thereby strengthening its governance framework and regulatory compliance practices.
BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Composition
The Company believes that an appropriately balanced Board, 
comprising Executive, Non-Executive, and Independent Directors, is essential to ensuring effective governance, maintaining independence in decision-making, and establishing a clear distinction between oversight and management responsibilities. In accordance with Regulation 17 (1)(b) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, hereinafter "SEBI Listing Regulations where the Chairperson is a Non-Executive Director related to the promoter, at least fifty percent of the Board is required to consist of Independent Directors. As on 31 March 2026, the Board of thirteen Directors, including two Non-Executive Nominee Directors, two Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors, eight Independent Directors (including one Woman Independent Director), and one Executive Director. The composition of the Board was in full compliance with the requirements of the Companies Act, hereinafter "The Act" and the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015.
The Executive and Non-Executive Directors on the Board are 
distinguished professionals with extensive experience and expertise in their respective fields. As on 31
st March 2026, 
none of the Directors held directorships exceeding the limits prescribed under applicable laws and regulations, including directorships in more than seven listed entities or ten public companies. Further, none of the Directors served as a member of more than ten committees or as Chairperson of more than five committees across all listed entities in which they held directorships, as determined in accordance with the provisions of Regulation 26 of the Listing Regulations. The necessary disclosures confirming compliance with these requirements have been received from all Directors. None of the Directors are related to one another within the meaning of the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.
The average tenure of an Executive Director (Whole-Time 
Director) is 2.66 years, Independent Directors is 3.38 years and that of the Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors, including Chairman, is 3.24 years.

The Board’s primary responsibility is to act in a fiduciary capacity and safeguard the interests of the shareholders by providing strategic guidance and oversight to the Company. In discharging its duties, the Board ensures that the Company’s vision, objectives, and business strategies are aligned with the interests of shareholders and the pursuit of sustainable long-term value creation.
The Directors perform their responsibilities with due care, 
skill, diligence, and independent judgment, while upholding

the highest standards of integrity and governance. 
The Board is responsible for setting the strategic direction 
of the Company, overseeing its implementation, monitoring 
performance against established objectives, and ensuring 
that management is accountable for the effective execution 
of the Company’s strategies and operations.
Responsibilities of the Board
Board Appointments / Membership Criteria:
The Company endeavours to appoint eminent and 
accomplished professionals from diverse fields to serve on 
its Board, thereby ensuring a broad spectrum of expertise, 
experience, and perspectives. The Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee (NRC), in consultation with the 
Board, identifies and evaluates the skills, competencies, 
qualifications, expertise, and experience required for the 
Board as a whole and for individual Directors, taking into 
consideration the Company’s business objectives and strategic priorities. The selection and appointment of 
Directors are guided by their professional competence, 
integrity, leadership qualities, and ability to contribute 
effectively to the governance and long-term success of the 
Company. Directors are expected to possess the requisite 
knowledge, experience, and judgment necessary to 
discharge their responsibilities diligently and to add value 
to the Company’s growth and sustainable development.
Based on the disclosures submitted by all Independent 
Directors and the Board’s due assessment of their accuracy, 
the Board is of the opinion that the Independent Directors 
meet the requirements outlined in the Companies Act, 2013 
and the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 and are independent 
of the management.
The table below summarizes the key qualifications, skills and 
attributes which are taken into consideration while nominating 
individuals as Board members:
Nature of skill, expertise and competence required by the members of the Board
Corporate Governance The Board and its Directors are expected to possess the requisite knowledge, expertise, and 
understanding to effectively guide the Company in the achievement of its strategic objectives while 
ensuring that its operations are conducted in a responsible, compliant, efficient, and sustainable 
manner. This encompasses a thorough understanding of corporate governance principles, applicable 
laws, regulations, governance frameworks, and industry best practices, as well as a clear appreciation 
of the roles, duties, responsibilities, and accountability of individual Directors and the Board 
collectively.
Leadership and 
Stakeholder RelationsIt is essential to possess the ability to provide effective leadership, cultivate constructive relationships 
with stakeholders, and drive organizational performance in a manner that is aligned with the Company’s 
strategic objectives, core values, and long-term vision.
Strategy Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of market dynamics, including the evolving needs 
and expectations of retail customers, with a strong focus on delivering customer-centric solutions 
and services. Directors should possess sound commercial acumen, an appreciation of the balance 
between risk and return, and a thorough understanding of the Company’s competitive landscape, 
strategic opportunities, and business challenges. Additionally, they should exhibit awareness of 
emerging trends, innovative business practices, and alternative or disruptive business models that 
may influence the industry and the Company’s long-term growth prospects.
Finance / Technical Directors should possess the requisite financial acumen to evaluate the Company’s financial position 
and provide strategic guidance to enhance financial performance, maintain financial stability, and 
support sustainable long-term growth. This includes the ability to analyze and interpret financial 
statements, accounts, and key financial indicators to assess the overall financial health and 
performance of the organization. A comprehensive understanding of financial matters is essential, 
encompassing areas such as housing finance, financial products and schemes, banking operations, 
funding and capital management, including debt and equity instruments, capital markets, the 
regulatory landscape, and the applicable legal and statutory frameworks governing the financial 
services sector.
Strategic thinking Demonstrate the ability to effectively identify and evaluate opportunities and risks arising from 
both the internal and external business environment. Directors should contribute to the formulation 
and assessment of strategic alternatives and provide innovative, forward-looking perspectives to 
support informed decision-making. They should also possess the capability to assess the potential 
implications of key business decisions, develop appropriate contingency measures, and promote the 
implementation of robust risk management and mitigation frameworks to safeguard the Company’s 
interests and support sustainable growth.

Nature of skill, expertise and competence required by the members of the Board
Analysis and use of 
informationDemonstrate the ability to proactively obtain relevant, accurate, and timely information from a variety 
of credible sources and effectively assimilate, analyze, and synthesize financial, technical, operational, 
and qualitative data. Directors should possess the capability to evaluate complex information critically 
and communicate key insights in a clear, concise, and understandable manner to facilitate informed 
decision-making.
Decision making Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate proposals and business initiatives against established 
policies, standard operating procedures, regulatory requirements, and existing business frameworks. 
This includes assessing the merits, risks, and potential implications of alternative courses of action, 
exercising sound judgment in situations involving uncertainty, and making informed decisions 
that align with the Company’s strategic objectives. Directors should also possess the capability 
to undertake prudent risk-taking while ensuring the protection and advancement of the Company’s 
commercial and stakeholder interests.
Communication Demonstrate strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to listen attentively 
and objectively, engage in constructive discussions, and articulate views in a clear, concise, and 
effective manner. Directors should be capable of conveying complex information and perspectives 
with clarity, thereby facilitating meaningful dialogue and informed decision-making.
Leadership Demonstrate effective leadership capabilities that enable Directors to address complex challenges, 
manage periods of change and uncertainty, and provide strategic direction to the organization. 
Directors should exhibit confidence, sound judgment, and conviction in decision-making, while 
fostering a culture that reflects the Company’s values and objectives. They should also inspire, 
support, and motivate stakeholders through their leadership, promoting collaboration, accountability, 
and organizational excellence.
Influencing Demonstrate the ability to build and maintain effective relationships and networks both within and 
outside the organization, fostering constructive engagement with a diverse range of stakeholders. 
Directors should possess strong influencing and interpersonal skills, enabling them to communicate 
persuasively and collaborate effectively across different levels of authority and responsibility. They 
should be adept at understanding the interests, expectations, and influence of internal and external 
stakeholders, while exercising sound judgment, stakeholder management skills, and organizational 
awareness in navigating complex business and governance environments.
Ethical Directors should uphold the highest standards of integrity, ethics, and professional conduct in 
the discharge of their duties. They are expected to act in the best interests of the Company and 
its stakeholders at all times, placing the organization’s interests above personal considerations. 
Directors should promptly identify, disclose, and appropriately manage any actual, potential, or 
perceived conflicts of interest, whether arising from personal, professional, or external relationships, 
in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and the Company’s governance framework.
Professional Directors are expected to demonstrate a high degree of professionalism in the discharge of their 
responsibilities and maintain the highest standards of skill, care, diligence, and ethical conduct. They 
should take ownership of their actions and decisions, uphold accountability for their performance 
and contributions to the Board, and support the achievement of the Company’s objectives through 
responsible stewardship. Directors should also act as credible ambassadors of the Company, 
fostering confidence among stakeholders and promoting the organization’s values, reputation, and 
interests both within and outside the organization.
Performance Oriented Directors are expected to remain focused on advancing the Company’s strategic vision and achieving 
the objectives established by the Board. They should actively identify and evaluate opportunities 
to strengthen the Company’s market position, operational effectiveness, and long-term sustainable 
growth. In carrying out their responsibilities, Directors should promote a high-performance culture by 
encouraging excellence, accountability, and the achievement of ambitious yet realistic goals. They 
should also support an environment that values continuous learning, innovation, and professional 
development, thereby contributing to the sustained success of the organization.
Independent Directors should demonstrate independence of thought and judgment, with the ability to express 
objective views and constructively challenge prevailing opinions when necessary. They are expected 
to encourage robust and meaningful deliberations by embracing diverse perspectives and fostering an 
environment of open dialogue. Directors should approach issues with intellectual curiosity, critically 
evaluate assumptions, and rigorously assess alternative viewpoints and proposals. They should also 
be willing to challenge conventional practices and support innovative approaches that contribute to 
effective governance and the long-term success of the Company.

The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC), in

succession planning process for appointments to the Board and

effective oversight and strategic guidance in advancing the 
Company’s long-term objectives. Furthermore, the Company 
emphasizes internal leadership development by providing 
growth opportunities for senior management, thereby fostering 
a strong talent pipeline and encouraging employees to aspire 
to and prepare for future leadership roles.
As part of its succession planning framework and to ensure 
leadership continuity, organizational stability, and the effective 
execution of long-term business strategies, the Board has 
approved a structured transition process for the position of 
Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO). 
Under this framework, a senior official from LIC of India may 
be deputed to the Company as Chief Operating Officer (COO) 
at least four to six months prior to the retirement, elevation, 
or transfer of the incumbent MD & CEO. This transition period 
is intended to facilitate a smooth transfer of responsibilities 
and institutional knowledge, enabling the designated 
COO to subsequently assume the role of MD & CEO upon 
the retirement, elevation, or transfer of the incumbent, 
thereby ensuring continuity in leadership and the sustained 
implementation of the Company’s strategic objectives.
In terms of Article 138(b) of the Articles of Association of 
Company, LIC of India is entitled to nominate upto one third 
of the total number of directors on the Board of the Company.

Nominee Director with effect from 13th June, 2025 and Shri R 
Doraiswamy as Nominee Director (Chairman) with effect from

FRAUD MONITORING COMMITTEE:
Pursuant to the requirements of the Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) (including Housing Finance Companies) issued by the Reserve Bank of India dated July 15, 2024, requiring the constitution of special committee of Board for Monitoring and review of Frauds, the Board has constituted this Committee to be named as Fraud Monitoring Committee (“FMC”).
The Fraud Monitoring Committee has been constituted to 
oversee and monitor fraud-related cases and to strengthen the Company’s fraud risk management framework. The Committee is responsible for enhancing fraud risk governance, ensuring effective detection and reporting of fraudulent activities, reviewing and monitoring fraud cases, establishing accountability, evaluating corrective and remedial actions, and recommending preventive measures to mitigate fraud risks and safeguard the interests of the Company.
This Committee comprises of 2 Independent Directors 
including 1 women Director and Managing Director cum CEO.

SETTLEMENT COMMITTEE
The role of the Settlement Committee (“STC”) of LIC Housing 
Finance Ltd. (“the Company”) is to examine and consider proposals submitted by the Recovery Department pertaining to loans sanctioned by the Executive Committee of the Board. The Committee shall discharge its responsibilities in accordance with the requirements prescribed under the Framework for Compromise Settlements and Technical Write-offs issued by the Reserve Bank of India on 8 June 2023. This Committee has been constituted pursuant to the authority delegated by the Board of Directors of the Company (“the Board”) and shall exercise its functions within the scope of such delegated powers.
This Committee has been established to provide an efficient, 
fair, and cost-effective mechanism for resolving disputes and disagreements between parties. Its primary objective is to facilitate amicable settlements through constructive dialogue, negotiation, and mutual understanding, thereby minimizing the need for prolonged and costly legal proceedings. By promoting collaborative problem-solving and encouraging compromise, the Committee helps ensure timely dispute resolution, optimizes the use of resources, and supports the achievement of mutually acceptable outcomes for all parties involved.
This Committee consists of three Independent Directors and 
1 Non-Independent Directors.

MEETING OF INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS:
During the FY 2025-26 two separate meeting of the 
Independent Directors of the Company were convened on 
11th December, 2025 and 25th March, 2026 respectively. 
During these meetings, the Independent Directors evaluated 
the performance of the Non-Independent Directors and the 
Board as a whole. They also assessed the performance of 
the Chairman of the Company, taking into consideration the 
feedback from both Executive and Non-Executive Directors. 
Furthermore, the Independent Directors reviewed the 
adequacy, quality, and timeliness of the flow of information 
between the management and the Board, essential for the 
Board to discharge its duties effectively and responsibly.
ANNUAL EVALUATION MADE BY THE BOARD OF ITS 
OWN PERFORMANCE:
In order to enhance the effectiveness of the Board, its 
Committees, and individual Directors, and in compliance 
with applicable regulatory requirements, a formal and 
comprehensive evaluation process is carried out on 
an annual basis.
The performance of the Board was evaluated based on 
feedback received from all Directors, using parameters that 
included the composition and structure of the Board, the 
effectiveness of its processes and functioning, the quality of 
disclosures and communication, and the availability of timely, 
accurate, and relevant information.
The performance of the Committee was evaluated based on 
feedback received from its members, with due consideration 
given to parameters such as its composition, the effectiveness 
of its meetings, and its overall functioning.
The performance of each individual Director was evaluated 
by the Board and the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee (NRC) based on various parameters, including 
their contributions to Board and Committee meetings. 
The assessment considered factors such as preparedness 
on agenda items, the quality and constructiveness of inputs 
provided, the ability to articulate and present views effectively, 
and consistency in upholding positions. In addition, the 
performance of the Chairman was specifically assessed 
with reference to the key responsibilities associated with his 
leadership role.The performance of the Independent Directors was 
evaluated through a structured questionnaire, wherein the 
Non-Independent Directors provided feedback on various 
attributes, including the skills, expertise, and experience of 
the Independent Directors. This process also contributed to 
the overall assessment of the Board’s performance for the 
financial year 2025–26.
The Board acknowledges and appreciates the commitment 
of the Independent Directors in safeguarding the interests 
of the Company and its stakeholders. Leveraging their 
diverse expertise, experience, and sound judgment, they 
make significant contributions to the Company’s overall 
performance. Their independent viewpoints, supported by 
extensive prior experience, enable them to provide objective 
and valuable insights as well as strategic guidance, thereby 
supporting the Company’s growth and development. 
The Independent Directors continue to remain fully committed 
and devote adequate time towards the effective discharge of 
their responsibilities.

DISCLOSURES:
There were no material transactions with related parties that 
may have potential conflict of interest with the Company. Details of related party transactions entered into by the Company are included in the notes forming part of the financial statements.
The details of all transactions with Related Parties, in the 
manner required, were tabled before the Audit Committee as per the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015, on quarterly basis during Financial Year 2025-26. The policy on dealing with Related Party transactions and procedures is disclosed on the Company’s website (https://www.lichousing.com/consolidated-related) and Related Party Transactions are appended to the Directors’ Report.
The Company and its subsidiaries have not given any loans or 
advances in the nature of loans to the firms/ companies in which directors of the Company are interested.
The Company has laid down the procedures to inform Board 
Members about the risk assessment and minimization procedures and the Board reviews the Risk Management report on quarterly basis.The Company has a Code of Conduct for prevention of insider trading known as “LICHFL Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading” in the shares and securities of the Company by its Directors and designated persons.
Pursuant to the provisions of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015, and the clarifications issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) from time to time, the Company has adopted the LIC HFL Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading. The Code is applicable to Designated Persons, their immediate relatives, and other Connected Persons, as defined under the applicable regulations. In accordance with the Code, such persons are prohibited from trading in the Company’s securities during the trading window closure periods notified by the Company from time to time and while in possession of any Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) relating to the Company. The Company has established appropriate internal controls and compliance mechanisms to ensure adherence to the applicable regulatory requirements governing insider trading.
The Company has a Code of Conduct for its Directors and 
the Senior Management. The Code includes the duties of Independent Directors as laid down in the Companies Act, 2013.

c. A brief on types of customer
s
The company serves a diverse customer base across the housing finance sector. The key types of customers include:
1. Retail Home Loan Bor
rowers:
This segment comprises individuals—salaried employees, professionals, self-employed persons and non-residentIndians (NRIs)—who avail loans to purchase, construct, extend or renovate residential properties, or who borrowagainst property for personal or business use. By serving diverse income groups and life stages, it advances financialinclusion and meets lifecycle housing needs, extending affordable credit that empowers families to own homes,improve living standards and contribute to sustainable community development.
2. Non-Individuals Bor
rowers:
This segment comprises corporates that borrow to purchase, construct or extend non-housing properties, oragainst non-residential property for business use, together with builders and developers seeking project finance forconstruction. Lending here is anchored in responsible project financing aligned with environmental safeguards andsocial-responsibility principles.

Governance and Ethics Risk and OpportunityRisk: Engaging in unethical conduct places organizations at significant risk, leading to reputational harm, regulatory sanctions, and diminished stakeholder confidence. For a financial institution such as LIC Housing Finance, where integrity and reliability underpin stakeholder relationships, upholding ethical standards is indispensable.Opportunity: A robust culture of ethics and governance not only enhances organizational reputation but also fosters greater stakeholder trust and drives operational efficiency. 3.
Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing
, recycling and disposing at the end of life,
for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste.
LIC Housing Finance Limited is engaged in the business of housing finance and related financial services and does not
manufacture or sell physical products. Accordingly, the requirement relating to reclaiming products at the end of life is notdirectly applicable to the Company in the same manner as it applies to manufacturing or product-based entities.
However, the Company recognises the importance of responsible waste management arising from its office and
administrative operations. The Company has adopted measures for reduction, reuse, recycling and safe disposal of wastegenerated through its operations, as detailed below:
a)Plastics,
 including packaging:
The Company discourages the use of single-use plastics across its offices and promotes reusable and recyclablealternatives wherever feasible. Measures such as reduced use of plastic folders and increased adoption of digitaldocumentation are undertaken to minimise plastic consumption in office operations.
b)
E-waste:
End-of-life electronic equipment such as computers, laptops, printers, scanners, monitors and other IT assets are
identified, collected and disposed of through authorised e-waste recyclers/vendors. Prior to disposal, the Companyfollows internal asset disposal protocols, including asset tagging and secure data removal/destruction, whereverapplicable. The process is undertaken in line with the applicable provisions of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.
c)Hazardous w
aste:
Given the nature of its business operations as a financial services institution, the Company generates negligiblehazardous waste. Limited hazardous or potentially hazardous items, such as batteries, toner cartridges and similaroffice-related consumables, if generated, are disposed of through authorised or certified vendors in accordance withapplicable regulatory requirements.

d)Other w aste, including paper waste, stationery, cardboard and general office waste:

4.
Whether Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is applicable to the entity’
s activities (Yes / No). If yes, whether the
waste collection plan is in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to Pollution ControlBoards? If not, provide steps taken to address the same.
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is not applicable to the Company. EPR obligations under the Plastic Waste
Management Rules, 2016, E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, and Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 apply toproducers, importers, and brand owners of specified product categories. As a housing finance company engaged in thebusiness of providing housing and other loans, the Company does not manufacture, import, or place any EPR-coveredproducts in the market, and therefore does not fall within the scope of EPR regulations.
While not classified as a Producer under EPR Rules, the Company disposes of e-waste and other waste generated from
its office and branch operations through CPCB-authorized recyclers/vendors, in line with its broader environmentalstewardship commitments.

10.Health and safety management system:
a.
 Whether an occupational health and saf
ety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). If
yes, what is the coverage of such a system?
Yes. LIC Housing Finance Limited operates a structured employee health-and-safety approach suited to a
financial-services institution. Although its core business of extending housing loans is largely desk-bound, theCompany recognises the health risks inherent in such roles and is committed to safeguarding employee well-being.
The Company’s health and safety management system includes the following key initiatives:
•
Pre
ventive Health Check-ups: Annual health screenings are provided to all employees aged 35 and above to
encourage early detection and prevention of health issues.
•Group 
Mediclaim Policy: Comprehensive medical insurance is extended to employees and their families,
ensuring financial support during medical emergencies.
•Ex-Gratia Reimbur
sement: Where the cost of treating a critical illness exceeds Mediclaim limits, the Company
may provide additional financial assistance on a case-by-case basis.
•Medical Lump Sum Allow
ance: An annual medical allowance is provided to all employees to support out-of-
pocket medical expenses.
•P
aid Sick Leave: Employees are entitled to paid sick leave, enabling them to rest and recover without
financial stress.
•F
irst Aid Readiness: First aid kits are maintained at all office premises to address minor health emergencies.
•Safety and W
ellness Programmes: The Company conducts regular awareness sessions and training on fire safety
and general health to foster a safe workplace culture. Fire drills, evacuation training and equipment inspections
are carried out periodically across locations to ensure preparedness and compliance with safety norms.
These initiatives are designed not only to ensure compliance with health and safety standards but also to foster a supportive and health-conscious workplace environment.
b.
 What are the processes used to identify wor
k-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by
the entity?
The Company conducts regular safety inspections across offices, including checks of fire extinguishers and elevators, 
and trains employees in emergency procedures and safe equipment use. Periodic mock drills for fire, earthquakeand evacuation scenarios reinforce preparedness, while wellness sessions and preventive health check-ups foremployees aged over 35 support early risk identification. A group health-insurance policy covers employees andtheir dependents.
c. Whether you ha
ve processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks.
As a financial-services institution with an entirely office-based workforce, the Company does not undertake hazardousphysical operations, manufacturing or fieldwork that would expose employees to occupational physical hazards.Formal mechanisms for workers to remove themselves from imminent physical danger are therefore not directlyapplicable. Employees may nonetheless raise any workplace-safety concern through the Company’s establishedgrievance-redressal channels.
d. Do the emplo
yees/ workers of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services?
Yes, the company prioritizes employee well-being by providing a robust healthcare program.

8.Does the entity ha ve any project related to reducing Greenhouse Gas emission? If Yes, then provide details.
Yes, LIC HFL is actively pursuing a range of initiatives to lower greenhouse gas emissions. Key actions include:
LED lighting upgrades: Conventional lighting across office locations has been replaced with energy-efficient LED fixtures,
improving energy efficiency and delivering a measurable reduction in carbon emissions in line with the Company’ssustainability goals.
Renewable energy procurement: From January 2025, LIC HFL began sourcing renewable (green) energy from utility providers
for twenty-two of its offices. By FY 2025-26 this initiative alone had avoided approximately 626.00 tonnes of CO
2e15
emissions,
 demonstrating the tangible impact of clean-energy adoption.
On-site solar installation: In March 2025 the Company commissioned its first in-house project, a 10 kWp rooftop solar16
pow
er plant. The installation reduces reliance on grid electricity, lowers the carbon footprint and reflects LIC HFL’s
commitment to renewable-energy integration.
AI-driven energy optimisation: An AI-powered module monitors and optimises energy consumption across selected offices,
using analytics to identify inefficiencies and recommend corrective action—improving efficiency through data-driven decisions.
Sensor- and timer-controlled lighting: Automated lighting systems across facilities ensure lights operate only when needed, 
cutting electricity consumption and operational costs while improving efficiency.

Opinion
We have audited the accompanying standalone financial 
statements of LIC Housing Finance Limited (“the Company”), 
which comprise the standalone balance sheet as at March 31, 2026, the standalone statement of profit and loss including other comprehensive income, the standalone statement of cash flow and the standalone statement of changes in equity for the year then ended, and notes to the standalone financial statements, including a summary of material accounting policies and other explanatory information (hereinafter referred to as “the standalone financial statements”).
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according 
to the explanations given to us, the aforesaid standalone financial statements give the information required by the Companies Act, 2013, as amended (“the Act”), in the manner so required and give a true and fair view in conformity with the Indian Accounting Standards prescribed under section 133 of the Act (“Ind AS”) and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, of the state of affairs of the Company as at March 31, 2026, its profit and other comprehensive income, its cash flows and the changes in equity for the year ended on that date.
Basis for Opinion
We conducted our audit of the standalone financial statements in accordance with the Standards on Auditing (SAs) specified under sub-section (10) of Section 143 of the Act. Our responsibilities under those SAs are further 
described in the ‘Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the Standalone financial statements’ section of our report. We are independent of the Company in accordance with the ‘Code of Ethics’ issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) together with the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the standalone financial statements under the provisions of the Act and the Rules made thereunder, and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements and the ICAI’s Code of Ethics. We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion on the standalone financial statements.
Key Audit Matters
Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgment, were of most significance in our audit of the standalone financial statements for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. These matters were addressed in the context of our audit of the standalone financial statements as a whole, and in forming our opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters. Subjective estimate – Expected Credit Loss (ECL) under Ind 
AS 109
Under Ind AS 109, Financial Instruments, the Company 
recognises impairment allowances on loans and advances using the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model. The ECL represents a probability-weighted estimate of credit losses over the expected life of a financial instrument and incorporates reasonable and supportable information, including historical default and loss experience, current conditions and forward-looking macroeconomic information.Our audit procedures included the following:
Understanding of the process and testing of controls•
W
e obtained an understanding of the Company’s
impairment methodology, accounting policies and
governance framework for Expected Credit Loss (ECL)and assessed their compliance with the requirements ofInd AS 109 and the applicable Reserve Bank of India(RBI) guidelines.

The Key audit matters How our audit addressed the key audit matter 
The estimation of ECL involves significant management 
judgement and estimation uncertainty. The key areas where we identified increased levels of management judgement, and consequently greater audit focus, are as follows:
•
Data inputs – The application of the ECL model requires
the use of large volumes of data from multiple sources.This increases the risk relating to the completeness,accuracy 
and appropriateness of the data used in
developing the assumptions underlying the ECL model.
•Loan 
staging and credit risk assessment – Significant
judgement is applied in determining whether therehas been a significant increase in credit risk sinceinitial recognition and in classifying financial assetsinto the appropriate stage under the ECL framework.This assessment considers various qualitative andquantitative factors, including borrower characteristics,internal credit risk ratings, repayment behaviour, remaining tenor, collateral valuations, expected recovery timelines,industry outlook and other relevant information.
•
Model estimations – 
The estimation of ECL involves
the use of inherently judgmental models to determinethe key inputs, namely Probability of Default (PD), LossGiven Default (LGD) and Exposure at Default (EAD).Among these, PD and LGD are the primary driversof estimation complexity and represent the mostsignificant areas of judgement in the Company’s ECLmodelling approach.
•
Economic scenarios – Ind AS 109 requires ECL to bemeasured 
on an unbiased, probability-weighted basis
by incorporating a range of possible future economicscenarios. Significant management judgement isapplied in selecting forward-looking macroeconomicassumptions, developing alternative economicscenarios and assigning probability weightings to thosescenarios, particularly in light of uncertainties arisingfrom geopolitical developments, inflationary pressuresand the prevailing economic environment.
•
P
ost-model adjustments (management overlays) –
Where considered necessary, management appliespost-model adjustments (management overlays)to reflect risks and uncertainties that are notadequately captured by the underlying ECL models.The determination of such adjustments involvessignificant judgement and estimates.•

e evaluated the design and tested the operating
effectiveness of key controls over the ECL process,including controls relating to data extraction and validation, model governance, approval of key assumptions andreview of the impairment allowance.

W

W

increase in credit risk (SICR), staging of financial assetsand timely recognition of impairment.

W

W
e evaluated controls over the identification, approval,

IT Systems and Controls
The Company’s processes relating to the sanctioning, 
disbursement, and recovery of loans and advances are highly dependent on automated controls embedded within its information technology (“IT”) systems. The Company uses a Loan Management System to manage its loan portfolio and process a significant volume of transactions. ANNEXURE B 
TO THE INDEPENDENT AUDITORS’ REPORT
Report on the internal financial controls under Clause 
(i) of sub-section (3) of Section 143 of the CompaniesAct, 2013 (“the Act”)
We have audited the internal financial controls with reference 
to these standalone financial statements of LIC Housing Finance Limited (“the Company”) as of March 31, 2026, in conjunction with our audit of the standalone financial statements of the Company for the year ended on that date.
Management’s Responsibility for Internal Financial 
Controls
The Company’s management and Board of Directors are 
responsible for establishing and maintaining internal financial controls based on the internal control over financial reporting criteria established by the Company considering the essential components of internal control stated in the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (“the Guidance Note”) issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (“ICAI”). These responsibilities include the design, implementation and maintenance of adequate internal financial controls that were operating effectively for ensuring the orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including adherence to company’s policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention and detection of frauds and errors, the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records, and the timely preparation of reliable financial information, as required under the Act.
Auditor’s Responsibility
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements of the Company based on our audit. We conducted our audit in accordance with the Guidance Note issued by the ICAI and the Standards on Auditing as specified under sub-section (10) of Section 143 of the Act, to the extent applicable to an audit of internal financial controls both issued by the ICAI. Those Standards and the Guidance Note require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether adequate internal financial controls reporting with reference to these standalone financial statements was established and maintained and if such controls operated effectively in all material respects.
Our audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit 
evidence about the adequacy of the internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements and their operating effectiveness. Our audit of internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements included obtaining an understanding of internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. The procedures selected depend on the auditor’s judgement, including the assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the standalone financial statements, whether due to fraud or error.
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is 
sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion on the internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements.
Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with reference 
to these Standalone Financial Statements
A Company’s internal financial control with reference to 
these standalone financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of standalone financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A Company’s internal financial control with reference to these standalone financial statements includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of standalone financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the Company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the Company’s assets that could have a material effect on the standalone financial statements.
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls 
Reporting with reference to these Standalone Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls 
with reference to these standalone financial statements, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference to these standalone financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial control with reference to these standalone financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.
